To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcriptome of wheat changes in response to cold.
cold acclimation involves the coordinated regulation of thousands of genes, and that the transcriptome profiles of cold-sensitive and cold-hardy wheat varieties are markedly different.
cold acclimation is associated with a major reprogramming of gene expression and this process is highly conserved across different plant species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how plants respond to cold.
understanding the molecular basis of cold stress responses and how these responses can be manipulated to increase the cold tolerance of crop plants.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the acquisition of freezing and cold tolerance in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acquisition of cold acclimatization and freezing tolerance is an active process that requires the reprogramming of the transcriptome.
cold acclimation is a highly complex and dynamic process that is mediated through the concerted action of many different genes.
the cold acclimation response is highly complex and involves a plethora of changes at the biochemical and molecular levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptome reprogramming in wheat during cold acclimation was similar to that in Arabidopsis and other cold-hardy species.
the transcriptome analysis of wheat has provided new insights into the molecular mechanisms of cold acclimatization.
the transcriptomes of cold acclimated wheat plants were reprogrammed to a great extent, and the expression of many cold responsive genes is different in the two wheat genotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptome reprogramming of cold acclimated plants is complex and is likely to be mediated through the coordinated expression of many different genes.
there are important differences in the cold response of cold-hardy and sensitive varieties.
